title: How Big Is the Universe? Every Distance to Scale

lines.text: Look up at the night sky. Everything up there is so far away, your brain can't even picture it.
But let's try anyway. One step at a time.
Let's start close. The Moon. It's about three hundred eighty-four thousand kilometers away.
lines.label: THE MOON

lines.text: Doesn't sound like much? When the Moon is at its farthest, every other planet in our solar system could fit in that gap.
Even light, the fastest thing there is, needs over a second to get there.
Now the Sun. You could fit about one point three million Earths inside it.
lines.label: THE SUN

lines.text: And it's a hundred and fifty million kilometers away.
Drive there at a hundred kilometers an hour, and the trip takes about a hundred and seventy years.
The sunlight on your face right now? It left the Sun about eight minutes ago.
Zoom out, and here's our whole solar system. Eight planets, all circling the Sun.
lines.label: THE SOLAR SYSTEM

lines.text: Light from the Sun needs about four hours just to reach Neptune.
Our most distant spacecraft, Voyager One, has been flying for almost fifty years.
And it's only now about one light-day away. One day, for light.
So what about the nearest other star? Proxima Centauri. About four light-years away.
lines.label: THE NEAREST STAR

lines.text: At Voyager's speed, getting there would take around seventy-five thousand years.
And that's just next door. Zoom out again, and this is home. The Milky Way.
lines.label: THE MILKY WAY

lines.text: Hundreds of billions of stars, in a disc about a hundred thousand light-years across.
And we're right about... here. Not even near the middle.
Our Sun circles the galaxy too. One lap takes about two hundred thirty million years.
The last time we were in this exact spot, the first dinosaurs were just showing up.
Our closest big neighbor is the Andromeda galaxy. Two and a half million light-years away.
lines.label: ANDROMEDA

lines.text: The light you'd see from it tonight left before humans even existed.
And the Milky Way? It's just one of hundreds of billions of galaxies.
lines.label: THE UNIVERSE

lines.text: By most estimates, there are more stars out there than grains of sand on every beach on Earth.
The part we can see is about ninety-three billion light-years across.
And nobody knows how big the whole thing really is.
And somewhere in all of that, on one tiny blue planet, there's you.
lines.label: AND YOU

lines.text: Watching a video about it. Pretty wild, right?
